questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer:
My motivation to go on exchange was to develop academically, but even more important: personally. 
To fully experience being independent of my supportnetwork of friends, family and learning how to navigate living on the other side of the world and making a new life for myself there.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To experience Australia has been a dream of mine for many years. Also, I find it a great advantage to visit an English-speaking country. Even though the culture is not too different from Denmark, Australia is something completely unique

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Going on exchange is the best thing I have ever done for myself.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
All the administrative work before going on exchange is super tiring and feels very overwhelming. But studenterservice can definitely help with a lot of questions, and the exchange inbound team at UniMelb was also very helpfull. But it is a loooong process, but when you go - it is all worth it. 
Reach out to older students and ask for their advice.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The inbound team at Unimelb offers a lot of information and they have an office (STOP1) where you can go for assistance and easily get an appointment. Here they will help you with everything from course registration to getting your card for public transport.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: This was the most challenging part of exchange - hands down! Everyone kept telling me to just go to Melbourne and find accommodation once you're there because the adds for housing can be super misleading. This is definitely true, but it is very difficult to find housing!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You need to prepare yourself for this process! It is super stressfull not knowing where you are going to life and spending your time at a hostel, not knowing if you are going to stay there for 3 days or 3 weeks. 
We had the best luck looking at fairy floss or marketplace (both on facebook). Here, private people post adds on their share houses (which is how most students live in Melbourne). 
Be prepared for people not answering you and be open minded. The official house renting companies are super overprices and tons of people comes to every single inspection, so don't bother wasting your time on those!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was very difficult to find housing on your own. 
The student accommodations available are SOOO expensive. But if you want something secure from the moment you land in Australia this is a good option.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Stop1 is super good at helping with everything

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You registrer in advance and then you are allocated through the UniMelb platform. When allocated you need to chose the specific sessions of the course that you want to join (they often have more than one) This way you can create your own schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop1

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If in doubt. Go to Stop1.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Based on the advice from UCPH I followed third year BA courses even though I am a MA student at UCPH. I found some courses were easier and some were harder than the ones I've previously had at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The most difficult thing about studying in Australia compared to Denmark is the continuous assessment. This means, that you have to 'earn' points during the semester that in the end accumulates to your final grade. Aka you need to perform well all the time, if you want to do well in the end. However, this style also takes a lot of pressure of the final exam that often 'only' accounts for 60% of your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australia in the Wine World (AGRI10039) 
Medical and Applied Immunology (MIIM30003) 
Experimental Pathology (PATH20003) 
Frontiers In Human Disease (PATH30003)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Australia in the Wine World (AGRI10039) 
Very fun and different. My 'non-serious course' I used my free elective course on. 
It is definitely work - so don't underestimate it. But we had wine tastings every week and I learnt a great deal of wine through the course and had a lot of fun. I would definitely recommend choosing at least one course outside your normal field of study to try something new and give your brain a bit of a break. This is an unique opportunity to do so. 

Medical and Applied Immunology (MIIM30003) 
Super interesting and really high quality lectures!! But SUPER difficult. Don't take this course if you haven't had any previous courses about immunology. I took 'Immunology' on my BA at UCPH and I still struggled with following the course. The requirements are super high so be prepared to work hard! However, I know that my interests lie within immunology so I definitely would have still enrolled in this course if I had to choose again. 

Experimental Pathology (PATH20003) 
Fun but quite easy lab-based course. With a background of a BA in Molekylær Biomedicin I had a clear advantage in this course compared to the Australian students. But ist was a fun way to meet a lot of local students since you are enrolled in a lab group that follows you the entire semester. We had to hand in reports every 14 days, but they were pretty straight forward. It just takes time. The work goes very in depth with a lot of fun topics like forensics pathology and looking at anatomical specimens. 

Frontiers In Human Disease (PATH30003) 
Super interesting and inspiring. A course that goes through 34 lectures basically covering a new disease every lecture. The lectures are presented by experts within each disease so there is A LOT of content to learn, but it is very interesting to learn about what is going on in research within each specific disease.

questions.answer: None unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: We had the pleasure of being enrolled in the 'food allocation programme' were you as a student would be allocated frozen meals every week! It saved us A LOT of money of food. The initiative was started during COVID but I don't know how long it will run for unfortunately

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the surf club and went to a few exchange events in the beginning. Unimelb has a exchange society called (MUSEX) that hosts a heap of events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go to the exchange (MUSEX) events in the beginning. 
Reach out to the students in your classes to get in contact with Australians. 
If you're single - go on a few dates. It's a fun way to meet people who knows the city ;)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit the nature around Melbourne but don't stress to much about needing to experiencing ALL OF AUSTRALIA. You won't have time to do it either way ;). 
Make peace with the fact that one of the greatest things about exchange is just experiencing actually living in a new city. Melbourne has SO much to offer so roam around the beautiful streets in the suburbs and enjoy life. Don't stress about needing to do everything all at once. And make peace with saying no.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy. Everyone in Australia are SO SWEET and welcoming! You can pick up a chat almost everywhere and a lot of people a genuinely excited to get to know you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go up and approach them. You have nothing to loose. And everyone is so nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No challenges.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Just the fact that everyone is so open, kind and welcoming. It is truly inspiring and something I would wish danish people also was.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make peace with the fact that you are not going to experience everything and that it's okay to say no. Don't let other people stress you out. 

Be prepared for the beginning being tough. I cried a lot in the first week and felt very far away from home. However, if anyone told me at that point in time that I needed to go through that one tough week to get 25 so absolutely amazing weeks I would do it again, without a doubt. 

Don't be afraid to take some changes and approach people. This experience is such a great change to challenge yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Ask the older students for advice - they have some great first-hand experience. 

Also. Stay at The Nunnery Hostel when you first arrive in Melbourne. The hostel is low quality and super cold in Aussie winter. But I met all of my friends at that hostel! So hang in there while you look for accommodation. 

BRING A LOT OF WARM CLOTHES! AND AN UMBRELLA! The weather in Melbourne is even more unreliable than in Copenhagen. And the winter is absolutely freezing - also inside the houses. I definitely underestimated the cold.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Challenging myself and realising that I am fully capable of being independent and creating a network of friends and feeling safe and at home on the other side of the planet.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first week. Where everthing was unsettled. I was struggling with finding accommodation and I felt very far away from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
DO IT, DO IT, DO IT! 
It is truly the best thing I have ever done for myself.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
